name: COCOS Translate
author: COCOS.

sections.description:
COCOS Translate makes your site bilingual without touching your theme or your content structure: it translates your site from its default language into one translation language of your choice. You can change the translation language at any time.

Core features:

  • Whole-page translation. The rendered HTML is buffered, parsed and every visible text node plus common attributes (alt, title, placeholder, aria-label, meta descriptions, Open Graph / Twitter tags) is replaced with its translation.
  • Live translation of JS-rendered content. A client-side layer (MutationObserver) translates content injected after page load – WooCommerce Cart/Checkout blocks, Gutenberg-hydrated blocks, AJAX fragments – using the same dictionary, and reports unknown strings so they get translated on the next visit.
  • Visual front-end editor. Open any page in edit mode, click a string, type the translation, save. Works for content, menus, widgets, theme strings.
  • gettext translation. Theme and plugin strings that pass through __() / _e() are translatable too.
  • Machine translation. Google Cloud Translation v2 with your own API key. Translate on demand from the editor, in bulk from the admin, or automatically in the background via WP-Cron. (Other engines are available in COCOS Translate PRO, a separate plugin.)
  • SEO-friendly URLs. The translated pages live under their own path prefix (e.g. /fr/). hreflang alternate links, x-default, translated <html lang> / dir and localized permalinks are handled for you.
  • Language switcher. Shortcode [cc_transla_switcher], a widget, a cc_transla_language_switcher() template tag, an optional floating switcher and optional nav-menu injection.
  • Built-in page cache for anonymous visitors so translated pages are served without re-parsing.

External services

This plugin can send text to an external machine-translation service. It does so only if you choose “Google Translate” as the machine-translation engine and enter your own API key under Settings → COCOS Translate → Machine translation. With the engine set to “None” (the default), the plugin makes no external requests.

Google Cloud Translation API (v2)

  • What it is / what it is used for: Google’s machine-translation service, used to translate the strings of your site (page text, menu items, widget text and similar) into your translation language.
  • What data is sent and when: the text strings to be translated, the source and target language codes, and your Google API key. This happens when you click the machine-translate button in the visual editor, run a bulk “Auto-translate” from the admin, or when automatic background translation (WP-Cron) or translate-on-access is enabled. No visitor personal data is sent — only the site strings that are missing a translation.
  • Service provider: Google LLC. Terms of Service · Privacy Policy · Cloud Privacy Notice

Links to translate.cocos.codes in this readme and in the plugin’s admin screens are ordinary hyperlinks; the plugin does not contact that site in the background.

Notes / limitations

  • URL translation uses the sub-directory method (example.com/fr/…). Sub-domains and separate domains are not supported.
  • On sites with a full-page caching layer in front of PHP, exclude the ?cc-transla-edit requests from that cache.
  • Very large string tables load into memory per request; let the built-in page cache do its job.

COCOS Translate PRO

This plugin translates your site into one language, with Google Translate on your
own API key. COCOS Translate PRO (https://translate.cocos.codes) is a separate
paid plugin for sites in several languages. It offers:

  • Several translation languages per site.
  • One-click AI translation through the COCOS Translate proxy — Google, DeepL,
    OpenAI, Claude and Gemini with no provider API keys to manage.
  • A monthly AI phrase quota with optional top-up packs.
  • Priority support and automatic updates from translate.cocos.codes.

PRO is optional and is distributed from translate.cocos.codes, not from WordPress.org.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the cocos-translate folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Settings → COCOS Translate, pick your default language and the language to translate your site into.
  4. Visit the front end, open the admin-bar Translate Page menu and start translating, or configure a machine-translation engine and run Auto-translate from the admin.
sections.changelog:
1.0.6

  • Fix: translated URL slugs are now saved as clean ASCII slugs, whether they come from machine translation, the visual editor or a manual edit (for example “categoría” becomes “categoria”, “Über uns” becomes “ueber-uns”). Accents are removed according to the target language and other scripts are transliterated.
  • Readme: added screenshot descriptions.

1.0.5

  • The plugin now translates your site into one translation language of your choice (Settings → COCOS Translate → Languages), changeable at any time.

1.0.4

  • Maintenance release.

1.0.3

  • Fix: language-prefixed URLs (e.g. /it/, /de/) returning a 404 on sub-directory installs — the language segment is now stripped without WordPress losing the site’s own sub-directory.
  • Fix: cached translated pages could be answered with a 502 by some proxies/CDNs because of an invalid HTTP header name on cache hits.
  • Fix: a stray XML declaration could appear in the served HTML of translated pages.

1.0.2

  • Compliance: documented the Google Cloud Translation external service (data sent, Terms of Service and Privacy Policy links) in this readme.
  • Fix: the live-translation collector now answers a failed nonce check with an error response instead of a success message.
  • Security: the text sent to the machine-translation engine from the visual editor is now sanitised on the server.
  • The platform moved to a new domain — plugin URI, update-check host, and every in-admin link (pricing, features, account, changelog) now point at translate.cocos.codes.

1.0.1

  • Fix: WooCommerce Cart/Checkout AJAX requests breaking on non-default-language pages.
  • Fix: a self-referential translation loop and corrupted HTML entities that could appear in some translated pages.
  • Fix: the visual editor no longer hides text that was already translated via gettext.
  • Fix: the WordPress core admin bar is no longer picked up as translatable content.
  • Improvement: rows in the languages table can now be reordered by drag-and-drop (the order also sets the language-switcher order).
  • Improvement: clearer, more visible outline around translatable text in the front-end editor.
  • Various translation-harvesting fixes and WordPress.org plugin-check compliance fixes (escaping, sanitization).

1.0.0

  • First public release of COCOS Translate.
  • Whole-page translation of the rendered HTML – visible text plus alt / title / placeholder / aria-label and SEO meta (description, keywords, Open Graph, Twitter).
  • Live translation of content injected after page load (WooCommerce Cart/Checkout blocks, Gutenberg-hydrated blocks, AJAX fragments) via a MutationObserver layer that also reports unknown strings.
  • Visual front-end editor: hover translatable text, click the pencil, edit the translation, save.
  • gettext translation for theme and plugin strings.
  • Machine translation with Google Cloud Translation v2 (your own API key) – on demand from the editor, in bulk, or automatically via WP-Cron.
  • SEO-friendly per-language URLs (/fr/, /de/ …), hreflang alternates, x-default, translated <html lang> / dir and localized permalinks.
  • Language switcher: shortcode [cc_transla_switcher], widget, template tag, an optional floating switcher and nav-menu injection – with bundled SVG country flags.
  • Built-in page cache for anonymous visitors.
  • Glossary with “keep as-is” terms; numbers handled as variables so “83 products” / “90 products” translate once.
  • Advanced tab with a “Danger zone” (delete all translations / reset settings).

screenshots.caption: Language Settings - Configure the default website language, translation language, SEO-friendly URL slugs, and automatic browser language redirection.
Visual Translation Editor - Translate website content directly on the frontend using an intuitive visual editor with highlighted translatable elements.
Automatic Translation Settings - Configure Google Cloud Translation API, automatic translation, background processing, and translation scheduling.
Language Switcher Configuration - Enable and customize the floating language switcher with a live preview and multiple display options.
Language Switcher Appearance - Customize background colors, text colors, borders, corner radius, flag appearance, and animations.
Language Switcher Position and Behavior - Choose the switcher position, width, spacing, flag placement, language names, and additional display settings.
Automatic Translation and WP-Cron - Schedule background translations using WP-Cron or a server cron job, and configure automatic translation limits.
Translation Limits and Progress - Set daily character limits, configure low-budget email notifications, and monitor automatic translation progress.
Translation Management - Browse, search, filter, manually edit, and manage collected translations from one centralized interface.
Translation Glossary - Define custom translations for important words, brand names, product names, and technical terminology to maintain consistency.
Advanced Translation Settings - Configure theme and plugin string translation, URL slug translation, caching, content exclusions, and string discovery.
SEO and Maintenance Settings - Manage hreflang tags, translation exclusions, cache clearing, stored translations, and plugin reset options.
